title: Applied Optoelectronics Signs $194.4M Annual Supply Contract With China's Yunnan Germanium
summary:
The U.S.-based optical networking firm has committed to a long-term supply agreement for the raw materials needed to build high-speed semiconductor components. Under the contract with a subsidiary of China's Yunnan Germanium, Applied Optoelectronics will buy 180,000 indium phosphide substrates every year from 2027 through 2031. The deal is valued at approximately $194.4 million for the first year alone, with the total cost for the 4-inch wafers estimated at about $970 million over five years.

The substrates are used to manufacture lasers for 800G and 1.6T transceivers, which are used by hyperscalers to expand AI infrastructure. The agreement remains subject to Chinese export approvals, and the company may adjust the volume of its annual purchases based on future market demand.
